candidates.name: Duke Energy Corporation
candidates.description: Both are major U.S. electric utility holding companies providing integrated energy services to millions of residential and commercial customers.
candidates.rationale: Same business model: large U.S. electric utility/energy infrastructure company serving similar residential and commercial customers.

candidates.name: Southern Company
candidates.description: Both operate as large-scale, integrated energy companies focused on power generation, transmission, and distribution across multiple U.S. states.
candidates.rationale: Same large regulated utility/energy infrastructure business, similar scale, similar customers and buyers; strong peer lookalike.

candidates.name: Dominion Energy
candidates.description: Both are significant U.S. energy providers managing extensive electric and natural gas infrastructure to serve diverse customer bases.
candidates.rationale: Both are large U.S. utility companies with similar electric and energy infrastructure businesses serving broad customer bases.

candidates.name: Entergy
candidates.description: Both function as integrated utility companies that manage power generation and distribution networks across large geographic regions in the United States.
candidates.rationale: Same business model: large integrated electric utility with generation, transmission, and distribution serving similar U.S. customer bases.

candidates.name: Xcel Energy
candidates.description: Both are major investor-owned utilities that prioritize large-scale renewable energy integration alongside traditional power generation.
candidates.rationale: Both are large investor-owned utilities with similar power generation, transmission, and renewable energy focus.

candidates.name: Evergy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both operate as regulated electric utilities providing essential power services and grid management to residential and business customers.
candidates.rationale: Same industry and business model: regulated electric utility serving residential and business customers with grid and power services.

candidates.name: CenterPoint Energy, Inc.
candidates.description: Both manage critical energy infrastructure, including electric transmission and natural gas distribution systems, to support regional energy needs.
candidates.rationale: Same utility/energy infrastructure business serving regional power and gas customers; comparable scale and buyer profiles.

candidates.name: Sempra
candidates.description: Both are large-scale energy infrastructure companies that own and operate extensive utility networks and energy delivery systems.
candidates.rationale: Large regulated energy infrastructure utility with similar scale, assets, and buyer ecosystem to NextEra Energy.

candidates.name: Exelon Corporation
candidates.description: Both are leading competitive energy providers in the U.S. with a strong focus on large-scale electric utility operations and grid reliability.
candidates.rationale: Similar large U.S. electric utility companies with overlapping power generation, grid, and clean-energy infrastructure focus.

candidates.name: AEP
candidates.description: Both are among the largest electric utility holding companies in the U.S., managing vast transmission and distribution networks.
candidates.rationale: Both are large U.S. electric utility holding companies with similar power generation, transmission, and distribution business models.

candidates.name: PSEG
candidates.description: Both operate as diversified energy companies with significant investments in electric utility infrastructure and power generation.
candidates.rationale: Both are large regulated electric utilities with power generation and clean energy investments, serving similar utility customers and buyers.

candidates.name: FirstEnergy Corp
candidates.description: Both are major electric utility companies focused on the transmission and distribution of electricity to a large customer base.
candidates.rationale: Both are large electric utility companies serving similar power generation, transmission, and distribution markets.

candidates.name: Eversource Energy Service Company
candidates.description: Both provide essential electric and natural gas utility services to residential and commercial customers across multiple states.
candidates.rationale: Both are large regulated utility companies serving residential and commercial customers with electric and energy infrastructure.

candidates.name: Ameren Corporation
candidates.description: Both are integrated energy companies that manage power generation, transmission, and distribution to ensure reliable energy delivery.
candidates.rationale: Both are large integrated electric utilities with generation, transmission, distribution, and clean energy infrastructure.

candidates.name: DTE Energy
candidates.description: Both are diversified energy companies involved in the development and management of electric and natural gas utility operations.
candidates.rationale: Both are large diversified electric and gas utility companies with similar regulated utility and clean energy infrastructure businesses.

candidates.name: WEC Energy
candidates.description: Both operate as premier energy holding companies providing electric and natural gas service to a wide range of utility customers.
candidates.rationale: Both are large regulated utility/energy holding companies serving electric and natural gas customers with similar infrastructure and buyer profiles.

candidates.name: PG&E Corporation
candidates.description: Both are major electric utility holding companies responsible for large-scale power delivery and grid infrastructure management.
candidates.rationale: Same business model: large utility holding company managing power delivery, grid infrastructure, and energy services.

candidates.name: Edison International
candidates.description: Both are large-scale electric utility holding companies focused on providing reliable power and investing in clean energy infrastructure.
candidates.rationale: Same industry and business model: large electric utility holding companies investing in power delivery and clean energy infrastructure.

candidates.name: Alliant Energy Corporation
candidates.description: Both are regulated utility companies that deliver essential energy solutions and services to residential and business customers.
candidates.rationale: Another regulated electric utility and energy infrastructure provider serving similar residential and business customers.

candidates.name: PPL Foundation
candidates.description: Both operate as regulated utility companies providing essential energy services and maintaining critical power infrastructure.
candidates.rationale: PPL Foundation is a utility-adjacent foundation, not a comparable large energy utility or renewable infrastructure company.

candidates.name: NiSource Inc.
candidates.description: Both are major energy providers that manage extensive natural gas and electric utility operations across multiple states.
candidates.rationale: Same utility/energy provider model; both large regulated gas/electric companies serving comparable markets and buyers.

candidates.name: AES
candidates.description: Both are global energy companies focused on accelerating the transition to sustainable energy through large-scale generation and utility services.
candidates.rationale: Both are large electric utility and renewable energy companies with similar energy generation and infrastructure focus.

candidates.name: Iberdrola SA
candidates.description: Both are global leaders in the energy sector, heavily focused on the electrification of the economy and large-scale renewable energy development.
candidates.rationale: Both are large regulated utilities and renewable energy developers serving similar power-generation, transmission, and clean-energy markets.

candidates.name: Engie
candidates.description: Both are international energy groups committed to low-carbon solutions and the acceleration of the global energy transition.
candidates.rationale: Both are large international energy utilities focused on power generation, renewables, and low-carbon infrastructure.

candidates.name: Constellation Energy Corp.
candidates.description: Both are major players in the U.S. energy market with a specific strategic focus on clean energy production and low-carbon solutions.
candidates.rationale: Same type of large U.S. electric/clean-energy utility company, similar scale, and overlapping customer and infrastructure market.
